reason: The text portrays elite figures quite favorably. Saul is described positively as 'bachor v'tov' (young and good), with no one better than him among Israel, and is explicitly chosen and anointed as king by God's prophet Samuel. His father Kish is introduced as a 'gibor chayil' (mighty man of valor). Samuel is portrayed as a respected prophet whose words come true. The people acclaim Saul saying 'yechi hammelech' (long live the king). While brief negative mention is made of 'benei beliya'al' (worthless men) at the end who despise Saul, these are not portrayed as elite but rather as base, contemptible figures. The overall thrust presents the elite positively.
